title: The past perfect
subtitle: The past before the past
review: Written by Claude in the format of the French tense pages. Check the examples and the level.
intro: You are telling a story in the past, and you need to go **one step further back**. The past perfect shows which action happened **first**: *When we arrived, the film **had started**.*

blocks.label: Earlier past
blocks.title: It happened before another past action

examples.fr: When we arrived, the film **had** already **started**.
She **had left** when I called.
I **had finished** my homework before dinner.
The train **had gone** when we got to the station.
By the time he woke up, everyone **had eaten**.

blocks.label: The reason
blocks.title: Why something was so in the past

examples.fr: I was tired because I **had not slept** well.
He was happy because he **had passed** the test.
The ground was wet. It **had rained** in the night.
She couldn't call. She **had lost** her phone.
I **had never seen** the sea before that day.
It was the best food he **had** ever **eaten**.
She **had** never **flown** before.
We **had met** once before.
She said she **had seen** the film.
He told me he **had lost** his bag.
examples.en: His words: “I have lost my bag.”

examples.fr: They said they **had finished**.
I thought you **had gone** home.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.formula: **had** + past participle  (the same for every subject)
blocks.note: The past participle is the same as in the present perfect: *finished, gone, seen, eaten, done*. Only *have / has* changes to **had**.

blocks.title: Two actions, two tenses
points: The **earlier** action: past perfect. The **later** action: past simple.
The order in the sentence does not matter: *I had eaten when he arrived* = *When he arrived, I had eaten*.
With **before** and **after** the order is already clear, so the past simple is often enough: *After I ate, I went out.*

blocks.text: already, just, never … before, by the time, when, before, after, as soon as, until, because …

examples.fr: I **hadn't seen** him before.
She **hadn't finished** when the bell rang.
We **hadn't eaten**, so we were hungry.
They **hadn't been** there before.
**Had** you **met** him before?
examples.en: Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't.

examples.fr: **Had** the film **started** when you arrived?
Where **had** she **gone**?
Why **had** they **left** so early?
**Past simple + past simple**: *When I arrived, she left.*
examples.en: First I arrived. Then she left.

examples.fr: **Past simple + past perfect**: *When I arrived, she had left.*
examples.en: First she left. Then I arrived: I did not see her.

examples.fr: **One past action only**: *I went to Bagan last year.*
examples.en: No earlier action: the past simple is enough. Do not use the past perfect alone.
